claims.text: Marajó is a large coastal island in Pará, Brazil; it is the main and largest of the islands in the Marajó Archipelago.
It is the second-largest island in South America, and the 35th largest island in the world.
With a land area of 40,100 square kilometres (15,500 mi2) Marajó is comparable in size to Switzerland.
Its maximum span is 295 kilometres (183 mi) long and 200 kilometres (120 mi) in perpendicular width.
The island is situated just south of the Equator.
Due to its location at the mouth of the Amazon River, archeologist Helen Palmatary compared the island to "an egg in the mouth of a snake".
From approximately 400 BC to 1600 AD, Marajó was the site of an advanced pre-Cabraline society called the Marajoara culture, which may have numbered more than 100,000 people at its peak.
There are large herds of domesticated water buffalo, which are technically invasive to the island; they now number about 450,000, higher than the island's human population.
Marajó is largely flooded during the rainy season because of higher water levels of the rivers along its coast and heavy rainfall in its interior; much of the island presents itself as a large lake.
